title: How Much Does an MTD Accountant Cost? What to Compare Before You Buy
excerpt: An MTD price only makes sense when you know which jobs it covers. A software subscription, quarterly filing service and accountant-managed package can involve very different responsibilities.
metaTitle: MTD Accountant Cost: Fees and What’s Included | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Compare MTD accountant fees, software, bookkeeping, quarterly updates and annual returns. See what to ask before choosing a managed service.
featuredImageAlt: A client examines a price tag while an accountant explains the records and filing work included in a service.

sources.label: GOV.UK — choose the right software for making tax digital for income tax
GOV.UK — choose agents for making tax digital for income tax

content:
An MTD price only makes sense when you know which jobs it covers. A software subscription, quarterly filing service and accountant-managed package can involve very different responsibilities.

Compare the work, not just the monthly number

Ask who maintains your records, checks transactions, sends quarterly updates and prepares the annual Income Tax return. Check whether software is included and whether the advertised price covers one business, several trades or rental income. A low entry price is less useful if you still need to arrange the work you expected someone else to handle.

Check TaxSimba’s current packages

Compare the current TaxSimba MTD packages and confirm the fee, payment frequency and service scope before purchasing. Ask whether the quote covers maintaining records, quarterly updates and the annual return for the same tax year, and whether the number of trades or rental sources changes the price. Keep the agreed package details with your records.

Ask about work from earlier periods

Joining after the tax year begins can involve records or submissions that need separate attention. Tell the provider what has already been done and obtain agreement on any additional charge before work starts.

Make a short comparison with four columns: ongoing fee, included tasks, your responsibilities and additional work. That is a more useful buying decision than choosing the smallest headline price.

A useful comparison example

Suppose one quote covers software access and another covers software plus maintaining records. Even if the first is cheaper, you still need to budget time or money for the bookkeeping. Write down the tasks you would otherwise have to do yourself before deciding which offers better value.

Questions to ask before paying

Does the price include the annual return for the same MTD tax year? Who deals with missing records? Are earlier periods included? How many businesses or properties are covered? When does the service start? Keep the answers with your purchase details.

Is a monthly fee the same as paying tax monthly?

No. The service fee pays for the work described in your engagement. Income Tax paid to HMRC is separate. For an illustrative fee of £29.99 a month, twelve payments total £359.88. This example is arithmetic, not a current TaxSimba quote or confirmation of an annual commitment. Check the live offer and payment terms.

Next step: Compare TaxSimba’s current MTD packages and tell us about your business and any earlier submissions.

Put it into practice

Compare a monthly quote with an annual quote

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

Imagine two quotes covering the same twelve months, income sources and work. Quote A is £30 a month plus £180 for earlier-period work: £360 + £180 = £540. Quote B is £420 including that same earlier-period work. Assume both figures include any applicable VAT and no other charges. These are invented comparison figures, not TaxSimba prices.

The headline monthly price is not the total cost. Before choosing, ask whether earlier-period work is actually needed and whether each quote covers the same service period. A different scope makes the comparison invalid.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
Monthly priceMultiply by the number of payments covering the agreed period.
Earlier-period workAsk which periods, records and corrections the extra fee covers.
Included filingsMatch each business, update and annual return on both quotes.

Two more questions you may have

Is the lowest monthly fee the cheapest overall?

Only a comparison of the complete agreed work and charges can answer that. Record one-off fees and any applicable VAT alongside recurring payments.

What should a written quote identify?

The tax year, income sources, record-keeping responsibilities, included filings, payment schedule and triggers for extra work.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Tax year and service dates
  • Income sources and businesses
  • Monthly or annual total including applicable VAT
  • Earlier-period work and agreed charges
  • Who maintains records, checks figures and submits

title: How Much Does a Self Assessment Accountant Cost? Compare the Full Service
excerpt: The right Self Assessment fee depends on the work you need, not simply the number of pages in a return. Before choosing an accountant, ask what the price covers and what could be additional.
metaTitle: Self Assessment Accountant Cost and Fees | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Compare Self Assessment accountant fees and what they cover, from preparation and review to filing, extra income sources and specialist calculations.
featuredImageAlt: A business owner and accountant compare income records and the scope of a tax-return service.

sources.label: GOV.UK — check if you need tax return
GOV.UK — legal financial

content:
The right Self Assessment fee depends on the work you need, not simply the number of pages in a return. Before choosing an accountant, ask what the price covers and what could be additional.

Compare preparation, review and submission

Check whether the accountant prepares the return, reviews your information and submits it after your approval. Ask how questions are handled and whether expenses, allowances or multiple income sources require a different package.

A fee for filing an individual return is not automatically a fee for business bookkeeping, a company return or a separate Capital Gains Tax report. Describe the work before paying.

Check TaxSimba’s current prices

Use TaxSimba’s current Self Assessment pricing to compare the fee and work included. Confirm which tax year and income sources the selected package covers, what review and submission work is included and whether any additional calculation needs a separate quote. Keep the agreed scope and price with your purchase details.

Ask about complexity early

Tell the accountant about rental income, overseas matters, cryptoassets, disposals and previous errors. A lower advertised fee should not be taken as confirmation that every specialist calculation is included.

Compare the total agreed cost and your own time commitment. An accountant who explains missing information before starting can be more useful than a headline discount with unclear scope.

A useful comparison checklist

Ask each provider to confirm the tax year, income sources covered, preparation and submission work, communication method and treatment of additional calculations. Comparing these answers is more useful than comparing the largest advertised discount.

Is the accountant’s fee deductible?

HMRC distinguishes business accountancy costs from the cost of preparing and submitting a personal Self Assessment return, which it lists as a cost you cannot claim. If one invoice covers different jobs, give the work description to your accountant so any allowable business element can be assessed separately.

Does a low price guarantee a refund?

No. A refund depends on the actual tax position, including income, allowable costs, reliefs and tax already paid. The value of the service is correct preparation and agreed support, not a promise to manufacture a repayment.

Next step: Review TaxSimba’s current SA packages and describe your income sources so the appropriate service can be confirmed.

Put it into practice

Compare the same tax-return job

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

Consider an invented £120 quote that excludes a separate £60 bookkeeping tidy-up and an invented £180 quote that includes the same tidy-up. Their totals are both £180, assuming identical work and any applicable VAT are included. A headline difference has disappeared once the scope is matched.

Now suppose the client also sold a rental property. Neither price should be assumed to include a separate property-disposal report. List that event before accepting either quote, rather than expecting a routine annual return to cover every reporting task.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
Annual returnIdentify the year and all income sources included.
Bookkeeping preparationCheck whether records must arrive reconciled or whether tidying is included.
Separate reportingAsk about disposals, historic corrections and specialist calculations.

Two more questions you may have

Does a higher fee mean more tax will be saved?

A fee does not establish entitlement to a deduction or relief. Compare the work and expertise required for your facts, rather than an unverified saving promise.

What if I find another income source after paying?

Tell the accountant before approving the return. Confirm whether the extra work changes the scope or price.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Return year
  • Employment, business, rental and other income
  • Record condition and missing documents
  • Disposals or earlier-return corrections
  • Preparation, review and filing included in quote

title: Joining an MTD Service Mid-Year: What Happens to Earlier Quarters?
excerpt: Joining an MTD service during the tax year does not, by itself, explain what happened to earlier updates. Your new accountant needs a starting position before deciding what work remains.
metaTitle: Join an MTD Service Mid-Year: Earlier Updates | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Joining an MTD service mid-year? Prepare your earlier records and submission history, check outstanding updates and agree any catch-up work before paying.
featuredImageAlt: A business owner and accountant organise earlier receipts alongside a trail of reporting calendars.

sources.label: GOV.UK — create digital records
GOV.UK — choose agents for making tax digital for income tax

content:
Joining an MTD service during the tax year does not, by itself, explain what happened to earlier updates. Your new accountant needs a starting position before deciding what work remains.

Separate three situations

Earlier updates may already have been submitted correctly. They may have been submitted but need review. Or they may still be outstanding. These situations involve different work and should not automatically receive the same quote.

Prepare a list of the update periods, whether each was submitted, who handled it and where the underlying records are kept. If you are unsure, say so. A guess can create avoidable work later.

What happens at TaxSimba

When arranging TaxSimba support, identify the update periods already submitted for the tax year you need help with. Share the confirmations and underlying year-to-date records. Your own description of a previous submission is useful starting information, but it is not independent proof that HMRC received it.

If earlier work needs correction, ask the accountant to explain the proposed work and whether it is included or separately charged. Agree that scope before authorising additional work, and retain confirmation of what is eventually submitted.

Ask about the full starting cost

Get a clear distinction between the ongoing subscription and any separately agreed catch-up or correction work. Do not assume a new monthly subscription clears every previous obligation.

Example: Q1 and Q2 already filed

If you join before Q3 after Q1 and Q2 were filed, give the incoming accountant the earlier confirmations and the records from the tax-year start. The next cumulative update still needs the year-to-date position; earlier records do not become irrelevant because the first two updates were sent.

What if I selected the wrong quarter?

Tell the assigned accountant promptly. Do not try to solve the issue by buying another package or making a duplicate submission. The declaration and work allocation should be checked first.

Does a payment unlock amend HMRC’s records?

No. An unlock permits work inside the service workflow. The accountant must then choose the appropriate correction or filing action using compatible software. Ask what has actually been submitted and retain the relevant confirmation rather than treating an unlocked dashboard card as proof.

Next step: Have your submission history and records ready when choosing a package, and ask for any additional work to be explained before payment.

Put it into practice

Joining before the third update: a handover example

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A sole trader joins a new service after two updates were sent by another accountant. The incoming accountant receives the earlier confirmations but no transaction export. Those confirmations show what was sent; they do not supply the underlying records needed to reconcile the next cumulative update.

The practical handover is therefore two-part: obtain the filing history and obtain records from the tax-year start. Agree who requests missing exports, checks the year-to-date totals and sends the next update. The example assumes standard update periods; confirm your actual accounting periods in the software.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
Earlier updates confirmedRetain the business, period and submission evidence.
Earlier records missingRequest exports and supporting records before treating the handover as complete.
Correction identifiedAgree who corrects the records and checks the next filing outcome.

Two more questions you may have

Can I start keeping records only from the joining date?

That leaves the incoming accountant without the earlier part of the tax-year picture. Arrange access to records from the start of the year.

Should I submit earlier updates again?

Check the existing filing history first. An unclear dashboard is a reason to investigate, not proof that every earlier update needs resending.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Joining date and next update deadline
  • Businesses and accounting periods
  • Previous submission confirmations
  • Year-to-date records and exports
  • Named owner of missing records and next filing

title: Can I Switch MTD Accountants Halfway Through the Tax Year?
excerpt: You can explore changing your MTD accountant during the year, but a good handover matters more than the date you move. The incoming accountant needs to understand both the records and the work already submitted.
metaTitle: Switch MTD Accountant Mid-Year: Handover | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Switching MTD accountants during the year? Use a handover checklist for digital records, submission history, agent permissions and the next filing deadline.
featuredImageAlt: Two accountants hand over a closed records folder while their client oversees the transfer.

sources.label: GOV.UK — choose agents for making tax digital for income tax
GOV.UK — authorising an agent to deal with your tax affairs

content:
You can explore changing your MTD accountant during the year, but a good handover matters more than the date you move. The incoming accountant needs to understand both the records and the work already submitted.

Start with a clear handover list

Ask your current accountant for the digital records, submission history, reporting periods and any outstanding queries. Request an explanation of how you can export or retain access to the records. Access to an HMRC account alone is not a replacement for the bookkeeping behind it.

HMRC supports different agent roles for MTD. The relevant authorisations must match the work your new accountant is taking over. Do not assume that ending a commercial arrangement automatically updates every permission.

Agree who owns the next deadline

Before transferring, write down which firm will complete the next update and which will prepare the annual return. Avoid an arrangement where each believes the other is filing. Tell the incoming accountant about any previous corrections or incomplete periods.

TaxSimba asks which quarters have already been submitted so the assigned accountant can review the starting position. A client-declared previous submission is different from work filed by TaxSimba.

Check the commercial arrangements

Ask about notice requirements, unpaid fees and any charge for reviewing earlier work. If corrections are needed, agree the scope and price before authorising them.

Example: moving after the second update

If the first two updates have been filed, the new accountant still needs the records from the start of the tax year. The third update is cumulative, so starting with only the latest three months can leave the new firm without a complete picture.

Can two accountants both be involved?

Different agent arrangements can be possible, but responsibilities need to be explicit. Name who maintains the records, who sends the next update and who finalises the annual return. Avoid asking both firms to submit the same work.

Will switching correct old errors automatically?

No. A handover transfers information and responsibilities. Reviewing or correcting earlier work is a separate question. Ask the incoming accountant to identify any concerns, explain the proposed work and confirm any extra fee before it starts.

Next step: Contact TaxSimba with your current reporting periods, submitted updates and available records so the handover can be assessed before you commit.

Put it into practice

A switch with two accountants involved

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A landlord appoints a new accountant while the former firm is still preparing an update. A commercial engagement letter alone does not establish who now has the appropriate HMRC permissions or who will send the work already in progress.

Write a handover note naming the owner of the next update and annual return. Match permissions to the agreed roles and obtain records and filing evidence. If the old firm will finish a specific task, record that boundary explicitly; avoid two people independently submitting the same work.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
RecordsAgree export format, period covered and delivery date.
PermissionsCheck the relevant main or supporting-agent authorisation.
Work in progressName the person responsible for checking and sending each outstanding task.

Two more questions you may have

Is cancelling the old engagement enough?

No. Commercial arrangements, access permissions and outstanding filing tasks each need attention.

What if the two firms disagree about what was filed?

Compare the submission evidence and HMRC activity before taking another filing action. Keep the resolution with the handover record.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Old and new accountant contact details
  • Handover date
  • Work completed and submission evidence
  • Outstanding tasks with named owners
  • Record exports and authorisation status

title: Does MTD Mean Paying Income Tax Every Quarter?
excerpt: Quarterly MTD updates are not automatically quarterly tax bills. Reporting your business information and paying your Income Tax are separate parts of the process.
metaTitle: Does MTD Mean Quarterly Income Tax Payments? | TaxSimba
metaDescription: MTD quarterly updates report your records; they are not automatically tax bills. Understand estimates, annual returns and separate Income Tax payment dates.
featuredImageAlt: A sole trader and accountant separate a reporting calendar from a savings jar used to budget for tax.

sources.label: GOV.UK — using making tax digital for income tax for the first time
GOV.UK — deadlines

content:
Quarterly MTD updates are not automatically quarterly tax bills. Reporting your business information and paying your Income Tax are separate parts of the process.

Understand the three different amounts

A quarterly update reports information from your records. An estimate can help you understand the possible tax position. The final annual calculation brings the relevant information together. Do not treat every figure labelled “estimated tax” as an immediate payment demand.

HMRC says the requirement to submit an annual return and pay by the following 31 January continues under MTD. Payments on account can also remain relevant, so check your own HMRC statement rather than assuming there is only one payment a year.

Keep your service fee separate

Your accountant’s monthly subscription is a payment for professional services. It is not an instalment of tax paid to HMRC. Check the recipient and purpose when you make a payment.

Use updates to plan ahead

More regular records can help you notice a growing tax liability earlier. Discuss a sensible reserve with your accountant, especially if profits change significantly. Setting money aside does not itself settle the eventual tax bill.

Example: an estimate and a service invoice

Your dashboard might show an estimated Income Tax figure while a separate invoice charges for accountant services. Paying the service invoice does not settle the estimated tax. Check who the payment is going to and what obligation it relates to.

Will my tax payment dates ever change?

Use your actual HMRC statement and current guidance. Payments on account, adjustments and individual arrangements can affect what you need to pay. A general MTD explanation is not a replacement for checking your own account.

Should I wait for the final return before budgeting?

Regular records can help you plan earlier, but the estimate can change as other income, reliefs and year-end adjustments are included. Ask the accountant what remains unknown before deciding how much to reserve.

Next step: Ask the accountant to explain your expected tax payment dates and service billing separately. If you already have a payments-on-account schedule, keep it available when you join.

Put it into practice

An update estimate is not a payment instruction

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A fictional sole trader sees a £2,400 estimate after an update and assumes a £600 payment is due immediately because there are four quarters. That division does not establish any legal payment obligation. The estimate may change as records and other income are added.

Keep three separate records: the update sent, the current estimate and the actual amounts and dates HMRC says are payable. A savings transfer you make for budgeting is your own planning decision, not evidence of a new quarterly tax-payment deadline.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
Quarterly updateCheck the reporting period and successful submission.
In-year estimateUse as provisional planning information, with its limitations.
Payment liabilityCheck the actual HMRC statement, payment dates and amounts.

Two more questions you may have

Should I divide the estimate by four and pay that?

Not as a way of determining what is legally due. Check the actual liability and payment timetable separately.

Can I put money aside monthly?

Yes, budgeting is separate from when HMRC requires payment. Revisit your savings plan as better information becomes available.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Update period and confirmation
  • Date and assumptions of current estimate
  • Other income not yet reflected
  • Actual HMRC payment dates and amounts
  • Personal tax-budget review date

title: Self Assessment for 2025/26 and MTD for 2026/27: Why Both May Be Due
excerpt: Starting MTD does not remove a return due for an earlier tax year. In autumn 2026, some people are managing 2026/27 MTD work while still preparing their 2025/26 Self Assessment.
metaTitle: 2025/26 Self Assessment and 2026/27 MTD | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Starting MTD in 2026/27 does not finish your 2025/26 Self Assessment. Track both tax years, records, services and filing responsibilities separately.
featuredImageAlt: A business owner and accountant keep a completed-year folder separate from current digital records.

sources.label: GOV.UK — deadlines
GOV.UK — using making tax digital for income tax for the first time
GOV.UK — submit your tax return

content:
Starting MTD does not remove a return due for an earlier tax year. In autumn 2026, some people are managing 2026/27 MTD work while still preparing their 2025/26 Self Assessment.

Put the tax year on every document request

The 2025/26 tax year ended on 5 April 2026. Its usual online Self Assessment filing deadline is 31 January 2027. The MTD updates you are working on during 2026/27 concern a different year.

HMRC’s first-year timetable puts the 2026/27 MTD annual return deadline at 31 January 2028. Do not move the earlier return into that later timetable.

Avoid paying twice for the same agreed service

When choosing support, ask which year the purchase covers. A package including the annual return for an MTD service year does not automatically include a separate earlier-year return.

Make a simple list showing each tax year, the accountant responsible, records still needed and whether the work has been submitted. Keep filing and tax-payment confirmations with the correct year.

Tell the incoming accountant about unfinished work

A previous accountant may still be completing 2025/26 while another starts the new MTD year. Both need clear instructions about their responsibilities so that nothing is missed or duplicated.

A simple two-row tracker

Create one row for 2025/26 Self Assessment and another for 2026/27 MTD. Against each, record the service purchased, accountant responsible, next action and submission status. This prevents an update about one year being mistaken for completion of the other.

Which records go where?

Label folders with the tax year and source of income. Keep employment documents and annual statements with the year they cover, not the date you downloaded them. If an expense or payment falls near the boundary, provide its dates for the accountant to assess.

Does signing one letter cover both years?

Check the purchase details and engagement. A reusable agreement can support more than one service, but the actual work, periods and fees still need identifying. Do not infer coverage from a generic heading alone.

Next step: Tell TaxSimba which tax year you need help with and whether any earlier returns remain outstanding before purchasing or adding a service.

Put it into practice

Two tax years on the same desk

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

In autumn 2026, a taxpayer can be preparing the annual return for 6 April 2025 to 5 April 2026 while maintaining MTD records for 2026/27. A folder called “this year” makes it easy to mix them up.

Label documents with explicit start and end dates. Give the accountant an employment certificate for the earlier return and a separate current-year transaction export for MTD work. Completing one task does not establish that the other has been filed. Check each reporting obligation and its evidence independently.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
2025/26 return recordsUse income and expense evidence for that tax year.
2026/27 MTD recordsMaintain the current-year digital records and update history.
Submission evidenceKeep a separate confirmation for each return or update.

Two more questions you may have

Does a current MTD update finish the earlier return?

No. It covers a different reporting task and period. Confirm the earlier return position separately.

Can one accountant handle both?

Potentially, if the engagement covers both jobs and the accountant has the appropriate authority. Confirm the years and tasks in writing.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • 2025/26 annual return status
  • 2025/26 missing documents
  • 2026/27 businesses and digital records
  • 2026/27 update confirmations
  • Separate owners and deadlines for both workflows

title: Are MTD Quarterly Updates Cumulative? A Simple Worked Example
excerpt: Yes. MTD quarterly updates report the tax year so far, rather than treating each submission as a separate three-month total. This distinction matters when you check what has been sent.
metaTitle: Are MTD Quarterly Updates Cumulative? | TaxSimba
metaDescription: See how cumulative MTD updates report year-to-date figures, with a £12,000 plus £15,000 example and checks to avoid counting earlier income twice.
featuredImageAlt: An accountant and client organise a growing sequence of records to illustrate cumulative reporting.

sources.label: GOV.UK — send quarterly updates

content:
Yes. MTD quarterly updates report the tax year so far, rather than treating each submission as a separate three-month total. This distinction matters when you check what has been sent.

An example of the difference

Suppose a business receives £12,000 in its first quarter and £15,000 in its second. Its income for the first half of the year is £27,000. The second cumulative update reflects that year-to-date position, not just the £15,000 received during the second quarter.

This is an illustration of income only. The actual update also depends on the business records and relevant expense categories. Your accountant or software should assemble the correct totals; do not copy the example into a return.

Use labels that tell you what you are looking at

A dashboard might divide your workflow into Q1, Q2, Q3 and Q4. That can be convenient for tracking work, but it should not hide the coverage of the submitted update. A standard second update covers 6 April to 5 October. Confirm the periods in use if you have calendar reporting.

What to check before approval

Ask whether the figures are a quarter’s activity or the cumulative update. Check that earlier records have carried forward and that corrections have not accidentally duplicated income.

Three checks before approving the figures

First, confirm the business and tax year. Second, read the start and end dates of the update. Third, compare the cumulative totals with the underlying records for that whole period. Comparing a cumulative total only with the most recent quarter is not a like-for-like check.

Does cumulative mean adding the submitted totals together?

No. If one update already contains the earlier activity, adding it to the next cumulative update counts that earlier activity again. Use the records or the latest appropriate year-to-date totals for the question being checked.

What about corrections to Q1?

Ask the accountant how a corrected record is reflected in subsequent updates. Do not assume every correction requires a separate resubmission of the original quarter. The stage reached in the tax year and whether the annual return has been filed affect the correct next step.

Next step: If the update looks different from your bank totals for one quarter, ask your accountant to explain the year-to-date reconciliation before assuming something is wrong.

Put it into practice

A cumulative update in numbers

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

Assume standard periods and one business. By 5 July, the records show £10,000 income and £3,000 expenses. From 6 July to 5 October, the business records another £8,000 income and £2,000 expenses. The second update covers the tax year so far: £18,000 income and £5,000 expenses, assuming no corrections.

Do not enter £18,000 as fresh transactions on top of the earlier £10,000. The software should build the cumulative totals from the underlying records. These figures illustrate record aggregation only; they are not a final taxable-profit or tax-bill calculation.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
First update: 6 April–5 JulyIncome £10,000; expenses £3,000.
Additional records: 6 July–5 OctoberIncome £8,000; expenses £2,000.
Second update: 6 April–5 OctoberIncome £18,000; expenses £5,000.

Two more questions you may have

Do I add the first two submitted totals together?

That would count the first period twice. Compare underlying records and the cumulative period covered by each update.

What if I use calendar update periods?

Confirm the elected periods in your software. This example uses standard periods and should not be copied without checking the period settings.

title: Found a Mistake After an MTD Update? How to Prepare for a Correction
excerpt: Finding an omitted receipt or wrongly categorised transaction after an MTD update does not mean you should start deleting submissions. First identify what needs correcting in the underlying records.
metaTitle: Correct an MTD Quarterly Update: Next Steps | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Found an error after an MTD update? Gather the evidence, correct the underlying records and check the filing stage before choosing the correction process.
featuredImageAlt: A client spots a receipt in the wrong pile and an accountant moves it to the correct records folder.

sources.label: GOV.UK — create digital records
GOV.UK — adjust your self employment and property income

content:
Finding an omitted receipt or wrongly categorised transaction after an MTD update does not mean you should start deleting submissions. First identify what needs correcting in the underlying records.

Make the issue specific

Send your accountant the transaction date, amount, description and supporting document. Explain whether the problem is missing income, an expense, a duplicate or private spending included as a business cost. Keep a copy of the original information so the change can be understood later.

HMRC’s guidance explains how corrected digital records feed into updates. The route can differ depending on whether the fourth update or annual return has already been sent. Your accountant should identify the appropriate stage before making the change.

Avoid correcting the same item twice

If a previous accountant is still involved, agree who will make the correction. Changing a spreadsheet and asking someone else to adjust the software independently can create two changes for one problem.

What happens if extra work is needed

Reviewing earlier records may fall outside the work already agreed. Ask the provider to explain whether the correction is included, what additional work is proposed and whether there is a charge. A dashboard unlock is an administrative step, not an HMRC amendment in itself.

A message that helps resolve the issue

Try: “The £240 payment dated 12 September was a personal purchase, but it appears in business expenses. The receipt and bank reference are attached. Please check the record and explain whether any submission needs changing.” This identifies the evidence without prescribing the tax treatment.

What if the mistake changes the tax estimate?

An in-year estimate is not the final annual liability. Keep enough information for the accountant to explain why the figure changed and whether other income or adjustments remain outstanding.

What if I have already approved the annual return?

Tell the accountant whether it was only approved or actually submitted. Those are different stages. A correction after submission needs assessment under the relevant amendment process; changing a local document alone does not update HMRC’s record.

Next step: Give TaxSimba the evidence and the affected period. The assigned accountant can assess the correction and request admin approval for any separately agreed work.

Put it into practice

A duplicate receipt discovered after filing

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

Suppose a first update included the same £200 business receipt twice. At the next update, the unreconciled records would show £7,000 of year-to-date expenses. Correcting the duplicate reduces those records to £6,800, assuming nothing else changes. Keep the receipt and an explanation of the removal.

This is a bookkeeping correction example, not a tax adjustment or instruction to amend an annual return. The filing action depends on the stage of the year and what has already been submitted. After the final quarterly update or annual return, check the applicable correction route rather than assuming a later routine update will resolve it.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
Duplicate recordIdentify the two entries and the one underlying receipt.
Corrected recordsRemove the duplication without losing the evidence trail.
Filing stageCheck whether a further update or a different correction process is needed.

Two more questions you may have

Should I delete the supporting receipt?

No. Keep evidence of the genuine cost and the reason a duplicate record was removed.

What if the annual return is already submitted?

Tell the accountant which return was filed and when. An annual-return correction is a separate procedural check.

title: Waiting for a UTR Before January? Steps to Take While You Wait
excerpt: Waiting for a Unique Taxpayer Reference is a reason to act early, not a reason to leave every other part of the return until later. Registration and preparing your tax information can involve separate tasks.
metaTitle: Waiting for a UTR? Prepare Your Tax Return | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Waiting for a UTR before January? Check registration, gather your tax-year records and tell your accountant about deadlines while the reference is resolved.
featuredImageAlt: A freelancer checks for a letter while keeping tax-return records organised at a home-office desk.

content:
Waiting for a Unique Taxpayer Reference is a reason to act early, not a reason to leave every other part of the return until later. Registration and preparing your tax information can involve separate tasks.

Check whether you already have a record

Tell the accountant if you previously registered for Self Assessment. HMRC’s guidance explains that some people may need to reactivate an account rather than start as a completely new filer. Follow the relevant HMRC process instead of repeatedly submitting applications.

Keep the registration date and any acknowledgement. Check HMRC’s current response guidance rather than relying on a delivery estimate from an old article.

Prepare the return evidence now

Gather income documents, expense records and details of other relevant circumstances for the tax year. Answer the accountant’s questions and identify missing documents. This helps reduce the remaining work once the reference issue is resolved.

TaxSimba allows onboarding without a UTR, but dashboard access is not confirmation that all filing requirements have been met. The accountant still needs to resolve the appropriate reference and authorisation steps before submission.

Tell the accountant about deadlines

Explain when you registered and which year is due. Do not assume a missing reference automatically extends the ordinary filing or tax-payment date.

What you can finish while waiting

Organise documents, identify income sources, answer onboarding questions and resolve missing-record issues. Keep a clear note of the registration date and the tax year concerned. These tasks can reduce the work still needed once the reference is available.

Can I submit without resolving the reference issue?

Onboarding access and filing readiness are different. Your accountant must confirm the required references and authorisation before submission. Do not assume that completing a questionnaire means HMRC has accepted a return.

What if I already registered years ago?

Tell the accountant before making another application. The appropriate action may involve finding an existing reference or reactivating a record. Use HMRC’s current guidance and keep correspondence instead of repeatedly applying and hoping one request arrives first.

Next step: Use HMRC’s registration guidance and share the acknowledgement with TaxSimba through the agreed document process. Never send your Government Gateway password.

Put it into practice

Waiting for a UTR without losing preparation time

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A first-time filer is waiting for their UTR while the usual January deadline approaches. They can still reconcile business records, collect employment evidence and retain proof of registration. Waiting does not make those preparation tasks impossible.

If registration took place after 5 October, check the actual HMRC letter: the filing deadline may differ. A later filing deadline does not automatically move the payment deadline. Share the letter and registration evidence with the accountant so the filing and payment positions are checked separately.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
Registration evidenceKeep the date, acknowledgement and correspondence.
Return preparationOrganise the tax-year figures while waiting for access details.
Deadline uncertaintyRead the HMRC notice and check filing and payment separately.

Two more questions you may have

Does paying for an accountant speed up HMRC issuing a UTR?

Do not assume a provider can control HMRC processing. Ask what preparation can proceed and what requires the reference.

Can I use a different reference number?

Do not substitute a National Insurance number or another identifier for a UTR where a UTR is required. Check the official process.

title: Employed and Self-Employed: What Your Accountant Needs for One Tax Return
excerpt: A job and a self-employed activity can belong in the same individual tax return. The accountant needs both sets of information to assess the complete position rather than treating the side business in isolation.
metaTitle: Employed and Self-Employed Tax Return Records | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Prepare one tax return for employment and self-employment: gather PAYE documents, business records and other income details for the correct tax year.
featuredImageAlt: An employee with a side business and an accountant combine two sets of records into one tax-return folder.

sources.label: GOV.UK — check if you need tax return
GOV.UK — what records to keep

content:
A job and a self-employed activity can belong in the same individual tax return. The accountant needs both sets of information to assess the complete position rather than treating the side business in isolation.

Bring the employment evidence

Gather your P60 or relevant P45, any taxable-benefit information and details of other jobs during the year. Explain job changes and any figures you believe are incorrect. PAYE deductions matter when the overall calculation is prepared.

Bring the business evidence separately

Provide income records, allowable-expense documents and the dates you started or stopped trading. Distinguish money earned from customers from transfers out of your salary account. Paying business costs from personal funds does not make the transactions disappear.

Use the correct tax year for both sets of documents. A calendar-year platform summary may need reconciling to the UK tax-year records.

Do you definitely need to file?

Use HMRC’s current checker rather than assuming every small amount of extra income requires the same action. Equally, do not ignore a notice to file just because tax has already been deducted from your salary.

What to ask before purchasing

Confirm that the service covers employment and self-employment together. Tell the accountant about other income, loans, pension contributions or property so these are not discovered after the scope is agreed.

Example: wages and freelance receipts

Keep your employment income and PAYE evidence separate from freelance sales and expenses. The return brings the relevant information together, but the bookkeeping should still explain where each figure came from.

Do I get another Personal Allowance for the business?

Do not assume each income source has its own separate allowance. Your accountant considers the individual’s overall position and the rules for the year. That is one reason the employment information matters even when your question concerns only the side business.

What if my employer already knows about the side work?

An employer knowing about it does not replace your tax-reporting responsibilities. Likewise, a business platform reporting information to HMRC is not the same as completing your return. Check the filing requirement and keep your own records.

Next step: Share both your employment documents and business records through TaxSimba’s document process for the tax year purchased.

Put it into practice

One return, two kinds of income evidence

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A fictional employee has £28,000 of PAYE employment income and a side business with £9,000 income and £2,000 expenses. Bring all three figures, the employment tax deducted and the business evidence. Do not report only the £9,000 paid through the business account.

The £7,000 difference between business income and expenses is only a simplified starting figure in this example. It does not calculate the final tax due, allowances, adjustments or National Insurance. PAYE tax already deducted is evidence to reconcile, not a reason to leave employment off the return.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
EmploymentP60/P45, relevant benefits and tax already deducted.
Side businessSales records, expenses, private-use explanations and accounting method.
Overall positionOther income and relevant contributions or repayments for review.

Two more questions you may have

Should I subtract PAYE deductions from business sales?

No. Keep employment income, employment tax and business records as separate inputs for the return.

What if I changed jobs?

Provide documents for the relevant employments and explain changes so the accountant can reconcile the tax-year position.

title: Uber and Private-Hire Driver Tax Returns: A Record-Keeping Checklist
excerpt: For a self-employed private-hire driver, the amount paid into the bank may not tell the full story. Platform deductions and different payment methods can make a tax return harder to prepare from bank statements alone.
metaTitle: Uber & Private-Hire Driver Tax Return Checklist | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Prepare your Uber or private-hire driver tax return with platform statements, mileage records and vehicle costs. Avoid confusing net payouts with income.
featuredImageAlt: A private-hire driver and accountant compare earnings statements, mileage records and vehicle receipts.

sources.label: GOV.UK — travel
GOV.UK — vehicles

content:
For a self-employed private-hire driver, the amount paid into the bank may not tell the full story. Platform deductions and different payment methods can make a tax return harder to prepare from bank statements alone.

Start with the full earnings breakdown

Download your platform statements for the relevant tax year. Keep records of fares, adjustments, fees and cash receipts where applicable. If you drive through several platforms or take other bookings, include those records too.

Ask the accountant to reconcile the platform totals to the bank deposits. Do not record a net payout as the full sales figure and then deduct the same platform fees again.

Keep vehicle evidence consistent

Provide mileage records and vehicle invoices or agreements. There are different ways to deal with business vehicle costs, and previous claims can affect the available method. Do not assume that fuel receipts and a mileage deduction can simply be added together.

Other costs need a genuine business connection and supporting evidence. Explain private use rather than labelling every payment as a driver expense.

Agree the scope

Employment status and working arrangements matter. Describe how you operate before assuming a particular tax treatment. Tell the accountant if you also have a job or another trade.

A practical year-end folder

Keep one set of platform summaries, one set of vehicle documents and one list of other business costs. Add explanations for transfers, refunds and unusual adjustments. Label every document with the period it covers.

Can I claim all vehicle spending?

Not automatically. The method used, business use, prior claims and the nature of each cost matter. Do not combine a mileage claim with the same running costs again without the accountant checking the treatment.

Does this guide cover every driver’s employment status?

No. Passenger transport can involve different arrangements. Describe who pays you, how bookings are accepted and the contractual position. If you are employed as well as driving independently, provide the employment documents too. The accountant needs the facts before selecting the return treatment.

Next step: Gather platform statements, vehicle information and a sample of your records before choosing TaxSimba’s SA service. This helps the accountant identify missing information early.

Put it into practice

Why a driver’s bank deposit may differ from earnings

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

Assume a fictional platform statement shows £1,000 gross fares, a £200 platform fee and an £800 payout, with no other adjustments. The payout alone is not the complete earnings picture. Record and reconcile the statement on the accounting basis that applies.

Do not start with £800 as sales and then deduct the same £200 fee again. Cash fares, tips, refunds or amounts handled outside the platform can add further reconciliation items. This simplified illustration does not decide employment status, VAT treatment or the deductibility of every charge.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
Gross fares in the example£1,000 before the stated platform fee.
Platform fee in the example£200 shown separately, subject to the correct treatment.
Bank payout in the example£800 to reconcile, not a second set of sales.

Two more questions you may have

Does every difference mean a missing expense?

No. Timing, refunds, adjustments and different payment routes can all affect the reconciliation. Obtain the statement breakdown.

Can a bank statement replace the mileage record?

A bank statement shows payments, not the business journeys travelled. Keep the relevant journey evidence separately.

title: Deliveroo, Uber Eats and Courier Tax Returns: Getting Your Records Ready
excerpt: Working across delivery apps can leave your tax information scattered between weekly statements, cash records and bank deposits. Organising it by platform is a useful first step towards a complete return.
metaTitle: Delivery Driver & Courier Tax Return Records | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Get your Deliveroo, Uber Eats or courier tax records ready: collect all platform statements, reconcile payouts and organise vehicle and work expenses.
featuredImageAlt: A bicycle delivery courier and accountant organise platform statements, work receipts and a mileage notebook.

sources.label: GOV.UK — selling goods or services on a digital platform

content:
Working across delivery apps can leave your tax information scattered between weekly statements, cash records and bank deposits. Organising it by platform is a useful first step towards a complete return.

Reconcile each app separately

Download the available earnings statements and keep details of fees, adjustments and any other amounts received through the work. Record the dates covered. Then match the statements to the money paid into your account.

Do not assume a platform reporting information to HMRC means your own tax obligations have been completed. Reporting by a platform and submitting an individual tax return are different processes.

Give the accountant the vehicle facts

Explain whether you use a bicycle, motorcycle, car or van, and whether it is also used privately. Keep relevant purchase or lease documents and mileage evidence where appropriate. The correct treatment depends on the circumstances and the method used.

Keep phone bills, insurance documents and other work-related receipts available for review. A payment is not deductible simply because it happened during a shift.

Include work outside the apps

Tell the accountant about another job, direct customers or other self-employed activities. Avoid sending only the platform with the highest earnings.

Example: two apps and direct work

A courier using two platforms plus occasional direct bookings should retain all three income records. A single annual summary from the busiest app is not a complete record of the activity.

Are platform payments already taxed?

Do not assume so from the fact that money arrived after deductions. Some deductions are platform charges rather than Income Tax. Use the statement to identify what was actually withheld and give it to the accountant.

What if I changed vehicle during the year?

Record when each vehicle was used and retain the relevant costs and mileage evidence. Explain any private use. Switching vehicles should not result in combining all the costs and applying one unexplained business percentage to everything.

Next step: Create one folder for each platform and the tax year, then share the statements and expense evidence with TaxSimba. The accountant can check the complete picture before preparing the return.

Put it into practice

Two delivery apps, one complete record

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

Imagine App A shows £700 gross earnings and £100 fees, while App B shows £500 earnings and £50 fees. With no other adjustments, the bank payouts total £1,050, while gross earnings total £1,200 and the listed fees total £150. Keep each platform breakdown.

If the courier also received £80 from direct bookings, add those records to the reconciliation. Do not use a platform’s calendar-year report as though it automatically covers the UK tax year. These are simplified bookkeeping figures; the treatment of each amount still needs checking.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act

Other workDirect bookings and other receipts need separate records.

Can I send only the busiest app’s summary?

That omits other work. Include all platforms and direct customers for the relevant period.

What if a report covers January to December?

Identify its reporting dates and obtain records that allow the correct tax-year period to be prepared.

title: MTD Software or an Accountant-Managed Service: Which Do You Need?
excerpt: Buying MTD software gives you a tool. An accountant-managed service also provides professional work. The right choice depends on what you can confidently do yourself and what you want someone else to handle.
metaTitle: MTD Software vs Accountant-Managed Service | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Compare MTD software with an accountant-managed service. Check who keeps records, reviews figures, sends updates and prepares your annual tax return.
featuredImageAlt: A sole trader compares a laptop ledger with the record-keeping and filing work explained by an accountant.

sources.label: GOV.UK — choose the right software for making tax digital for income tax
GOV.UK — authorising an agent to deal with your tax affairs

content:
Buying MTD software gives you a tool. An accountant-managed service also provides professional work. The right choice depends on what you can confidently do yourself and what you want someone else to handle.

Decide which tasks you want to keep

Write down how you will capture transactions, identify private spending, organise receipts and answer queries. Then decide who will prepare updates and complete the annual return. Software can support these tasks without taking responsibility for every judgement involved.

HMRC allows you to use an agent with compatible software. That does not mean every advertised software plan includes bookkeeping or an accountant who prepares your return.

Compare three practical arrangements

You might keep the records and submit using software yourself. Alternatively, you could keep the records while an accountant reviews and submits agreed work. A more managed arrangement can include maintaining records as well as filing. Ask which arrangement a quoted price actually describes.

Before choosing, consider the number of income sources, the quality of your existing records and how much time you can give the process. If you are moving from paper records or combining employment with rental income, explain that before accepting a quote.

How TaxSimba approaches it

TaxSimba is accountant-led. Check the current MTD packages and agree which record-keeping, review and filing work is included. You still supply complete information and answer queries. Compare the agreed work with a software-only plan before deciding on price.

A quick decision test

If you enjoy maintaining records and can give it regular attention, a self-managed arrangement may be worth considering. If you would prefer to supply the documents and have someone maintain the books, compare managed services instead. Neither option removes your responsibility to provide complete, accurate information.

Will an accountant need information from me?

Yes. A managed service cannot identify every private payment, missing cash receipt or change in your circumstances without your input. Agree how queries will reach you and respond promptly.

Will every software product handle my situation?

Do not assume so. Check the income sources, tax year and required functions against HMRC’s software guidance and the provider’s current capabilities. Where more than one product is involved, ask who is responsible for bringing the information together. A software name on a pricing card should not be treated as a guarantee of unlimited service scope.

Next step: Review the package description and choose the level of help you need, rather than paying for features you will not use.

Put it into practice

Choose a working arrangement, not just a product

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A landlord is comfortable collecting receipts but does not want to reconcile transactions or prepare updates. A software-only subscription may provide tools without supplying that work. A managed quote might include it, but the written scope must say so.

Compare the same list of tasks across each arrangement. Ask who resolves an unexplained transfer, checks incomplete rental statements and confirms submission. Calling a service “supported” does not by itself identify the person responsible for every task.

Two more questions you may have

Does software automatically check every tax judgement?

Do not assume so. Match its capabilities to your circumstances and identify the judgements you or an adviser must make.

Is “accountant support” the same as managed bookkeeping?

Not necessarily. Ask for the actual tasks, limits and responsibilities included in the engagement.

title: Authorising Your MTD Accountant Without Sharing Your Password
excerpt: Your accountant needs the appropriate authority to act for you, not a casual message containing your Government Gateway password. The authorisation should match the tax service and work being undertaken.
metaTitle: Authorise Your MTD Accountant Safely | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Authorise an MTD accountant through the appropriate HMRC process. Check the firm and permissions, keep passwords private and understand your responsibilities.
featuredImageAlt: A client uses his own laptop while an accountant explains a secure agent-authorisation request.

sources.label: GOV.UK — authorising an agent to deal with your tax affairs
GOV.UK — choose agents for making tax digital for income tax

content:
Your accountant needs the appropriate authority to act for you, not a casual message containing your Government Gateway password. The authorisation should match the tax service and work being undertaken.

Understand what you are approving

HMRC provides different authorisation routes for different services. For MTD for Income Tax, a main agent can finalise your overall tax position and submit the annual return. A supporting agent can help with records and quarterly updates but cannot submit that return. Ask which role is needed, particularly if another firm remains involved.

Read the authorisation request and check the firm’s identity. If something does not match the arrangement you agreed, confirm it through a known contact method before continuing.

Keep your sign-in details private

Complete your own part of the official process. Do not send passwords or one-time security codes by email or chat as a substitute for agent authorisation. If you cannot use the proposed route, ask what approved alternative applies.

Approval and responsibility remain important

Authorisation does not mean you should stop checking the information supplied for your return. HMRC says you remain responsible for your tax and must confirm the information is correct before an agent submits the return.

If you change accountant, review permissions as well as the commercial handover.

Signing an engagement is a separate step

Your client care letter records the agreed service. HMRC authorisation gives the relevant agent permission to act through the appropriate process. Completing one should not be treated as evidence that the other has automatically happened.

What should I check on a request?

Confirm the accountant or firm, the service concerned and whether the request fits your engagement. Use a known contact channel if the sender or wording is unexpected. Never approve a request merely because a message says a deadline is close.

Can I remove access later?

HMRC provides processes for changing or removing agent authorisation. If an arrangement ends, discuss access and outstanding work as part of the handover. Removing permissions does not itself complete a return, cancel a tax liability or settle the commercial contract.

Next step: Follow the authorisation instructions from your assigned TaxSimba accountant and use HMRC’s guidance if you need to check the request.

Put it into practice

An urgent authorisation message: what to verify

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A client receives an unexpected message asking for a one-time login code to “finish accountant setup”. Instead of replying with the code, they contact the firm through the number already in their engagement records and confirm the proper authorisation route.

The same check applies to a genuine-looking request from a different firm name. Verify the organisation and the requested service before approving access. The goal is to establish the agreed authority, not to transfer control of the client’s personal sign-in credentials.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
Known firm, expected requestCheck that the tax service and requested role match the engagement.
Unexpected sender or roleConfirm through a previously known contact channel.
Password or one-time-code requestKeep credentials private; use the official authorisation process.

Two more questions you may have

Does signing a client-care letter grant HMRC access?

It records the engagement. Check the separate HMRC authorisation step rather than assuming it happened automatically.

Can a supporting agent file the annual return?

That is a main-agent responsibility under the MTD agent-role guidance. Agree who will perform it.

title: Several Years of Unfiled Tax Returns: How to Put Them in Order
excerpt: If several returns are missing, start by identifying each affected tax year and what HMRC has asked you to file. A clear year-by-year record is more useful than submitting the latest return and hoping the earlier years disappear.
metaTitle: Several Overdue Self Assessment Returns: Next Steps | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Missing several Self Assessment returns? Organise records by tax year, distinguish overdue filings from disclosures and agree the work needed to get up to date.
featuredImageAlt: A taxpayer and accountant sort older paperwork into separate tax-year folders with a clear timeline.

sources.label: HMRC / GOV.UK — deadlines
HMRC / GOV.UK — corrections
HMRC / GOV.UK — let property campaign your guide to making a disclosure

content:
If several returns are missing, start by identifying each affected tax year and what HMRC has asked you to file. A clear year-by-year record is more useful than submitting the latest return and hoping the earlier years disappear.

Separate missing returns from missing disclosures

An outstanding return issued by HMRC, an incorrect return already filed and income never declared may require different procedures. Tell your accountant which applies for each year. A disclosure route can be relevant in some cases, including previously undeclared rental income.

Do not assume that one online form or a single amended return resolves every historic issue. The available filing and correction routes depend on the year and the facts.

Build a timeline of income and payments

Collect employment records, business accounts, rental statements, bank interest, gains and previous HMRC correspondence. Mark which records are complete and which need obtaining from employers, banks or former accountants.

For example, a bank transfer in May may relate to work invoiced in March. The accounting method and year-end treatment need checking before deciding which return contains it. Copying the same totals into several years creates further problems.

Understand the full amount due

The position can include tax, payments on account, interest and penalties. Filing an overdue return does not automatically cancel charges or arrange a payment plan. Equally, a penalty estimate is not a substitute for calculating the actual tax.

If payment is difficult, discuss HMRC's options while the returns are being brought up to date. Do not delay obtaining an accurate liability simply because you are worried about the eventual bill.

Agree the work before it starts

Specify the years, income sources, missing records and any disclosure or appeal work. Historic reconstruction can require more work than a current-year return, so the scope and additional fee should be agreed in advance.

TaxSimba can review an enquiry and confirm what it can undertake. Provide all relevant correspondence, including deadlines already set by HMRC, so the accountant can distinguish urgent actions from the wider task of getting your records into order.

Put it into practice

Build a year-by-year recovery plan

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A taxpayer has an unfiled return for one year, an error in a return already filed for another, and rental income never reported for an earlier period. Labelling all three “late returns” can lead to the wrong process being used.

Create a separate line for each year, describing what HMRC requested, what was submitted and what is missing. The accountant can then distinguish preparation, correction and potential disclosure work. The order of work should reflect actual notices and deadlines, not an assumption that the newest year always comes first.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
Return requested but missingIdentify the notice, year and outstanding filing task.
Return filed with an errorCheck the correction route and relevant time limits.
Income never reportedAsk whether a disclosure process is appropriate for the facts.

Two more questions you may have

Should I copy the newest year’s figures into older returns?

No. Each year needs its own evidence and the appropriate accounting treatment. Repeated estimates can create further errors.

Does filing settle every charge automatically?

Check the resulting tax, interest, penalties and payment position separately. An appeal or payment arrangement is another task.

  • HMRC notices and deadlines
  • Filed, unfiled or potentially undisclosed position
  • Missing income, expense and payment evidence
  • Agreed actions, fees and responsible person

title: Appealing a Self Assessment Penalty: Evidence, Deadlines and Next Steps
excerpt: You may be able to challenge a Self Assessment penalty, but an appeal needs the right grounds and supporting facts. Start with the penalty notice and keep the filing or payment obligation separate from the appeal itself.
metaTitle: Appeal a Self Assessment Penalty: Evidence & Deadlines | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Check how to appeal a Self Assessment penalty: read the notice, prepare dated evidence and explain your timeline. Appeals are usually due within 30 days.
featuredImageAlt: A taxpayer and accountant compare a penalty notice, calendar and dated evidence to build an appeal timeline.

sources.label: HMRC / GOV.UK — check when to appeal a self assessment penalty for late filing or late payment
HMRC / GOV.UK — reasonable excuses
HMRC / GOV.UK — tax appeals

content:
You may be able to challenge a Self Assessment penalty, but an appeal needs the right grounds and supporting facts. Start with the penalty notice and keep the filing or payment obligation separate from the appeal itself.

Check whether the notice is correct

Identify the tax year, type of penalty, issue date and reason given. Check whether the return or payment was actually late and whether HMRC had withdrawn any requirement to file. If no return was needed, asking HMRC to cancel the filing requirement can be relevant.

Do not assume that having no tax to pay automatically removes a late-filing penalty. The duty to send an issued return and the amount of tax due are separate questions.

A reasonable excuse depends on the facts

HMRC considers circumstances that genuinely prevented compliance, including certain serious illnesses, bereavements or service problems. What happened, when it happened and how it affected the deadline matter more than a broad label such as personal difficulties.

Explain what you did once the problem ended. Keep dates, medical or other relevant evidence where appropriate, service notices and proof of subsequent filing or payment. Avoid including unnecessary private information unrelated to the grounds.

Act within the appeal window

Follow the notice and HMRC's current process; appeals are normally required within 30 days of the penalty notice. If you are late, explain both the original issue and the reason the appeal itself was delayed. Acceptance is not guaranteed.

For example, evidence of a documented outage should connect the attempted submission to the actual deadline. A general screenshot taken weeks later may not establish why you could not file on time.

Resolve the underlying position too

Submitting the appeal does not itself file the missing return or settle outstanding tax. Check what remains to be done and whether payment support is needed. Also distinguish an appeal from a complaint about service quality.

TaxSimba can confirm whether appeal assistance is available within your engagement or requires separately agreed work. Send the complete notice promptly; no provider should promise cancellation before the facts and rules have been examined.

Put it into practice

Show how the event affected the deadline

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

For a fictional unexpected hospital admission, a useful timeline would record the obligation’s deadline, the admission and discharge dates, why the illness prevented compliance, and when filing resumed. A letter showing an admission months away from the deadline would need further explanation.

Use only genuine evidence and relevant facts. The example illustrates how to organise an appeal, not a prediction that HMRC will accept it. If the appeal itself is late, explain that delay separately from the original missed obligation.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
ObligationIdentify the return or payment and actual deadline.
Preventing eventExplain the dated facts and connection to non-compliance.
Recovery actionRecord what happened when the obstacle ended.

Two more questions you may have

Is saying “personal difficulties” enough?

Explain the actual event, dates and effect on the obligation. A label alone does not establish the grounds.

Does an appeal mean I can ignore the notice?

No. Read the notice and check payment, interest and the underlying filing position while the appeal is considered.

  • Appeal deadline
  • Dated factual timeline
  • Relevant genuine evidence

title: Sold a Rental Property? Check the 60-Day Capital Gains Tax Deadline
excerpt: Selling a rental property can create a reporting obligation before the ordinary annual tax-return deadline. Waiting until January to tell the accountant may be too late for a separate property report.
metaTitle: Sold a Rental Property? Check the 60-Day CGT Deadline | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Sold a UK rental property? Check whether Capital Gains Tax must be reported and paid within 60 days of completion, and what records your accountant needs.
featuredImageAlt: A landlord and accountant review property completion papers and keys beside a calendar and an hourglass.

sources.label: GOV.UK — if you sold a property in the uk on or after 6 april 2020
GOV.UK — reporting and paying capital gains tax

content:
Selling a rental property can create a reporting obligation before the ordinary annual tax-return deadline. Waiting until January to tell the accountant may be too late for a separate property report.

Tell the accountant when the sale completes

For a UK residential property disposal with Capital Gains Tax due, HMRC generally requires reporting and payment within 60 days of completion. Different circumstances, including non-residence, need their own check.

Do not treat a gain as simply the money left after repaying the mortgage. The calculation needs the relevant acquisition, disposal and allowable-cost information, together with any applicable reliefs.

Gather the property history

Keep purchase and sale completion statements, legal fees, ownership details and records of qualifying improvements. Explain when the property was your home, when it was let and any changes in ownership. Give the accountant dates rather than estimates such as “a few years”.

Ask whether there are two reporting tasks

A separate property report and an annual return can both be relevant. Confirm which work the accountant is taking on and whether it is included in the fee already paid.

If the sale has already happened, provide the completion date immediately. Do not wait until every supporting document has been collected before alerting the accountant.

A practical completion checklist

Record the completion date immediately. Gather purchase and sale statements, ownership shares, costs and the occupation history. Tell the accountant if you lived abroad or if another owner is arranging a separate calculation.

Does an outstanding mortgage reduce the gain automatically?

Do not calculate the gain as sale proceeds less mortgage repayment. Financing and the tax calculation answer different questions. Give the accountant the purchase, disposal and relevant cost evidence.

Can I leave it until the annual return?

Check the separate property-reporting obligation promptly. The ordinary January timetable does not replace a relevant 60-day requirement. If an accountant is preparing the annual return, explicitly ask whether the property report and payment calculation are included, and who is responsible for completing them.

Next step: Ask TaxSimba to confirm support and scope for the property disposal before purchasing a standard annual-return service.

Put it into practice

Completion date starts a separate clock

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

In a fictional sale completed on 1 October 2026, adding 60 days gives 30 November 2026. If the disposal is within the residential-property reporting requirement, the relevant report and payment cannot simply wait for the usual annual-return timetable. The example assumes no special circumstances.

Tell the accountant immediately, even if one invoice is missing. Provide purchase and disposal details, ownership shares and occupation history so the actual reporting requirement and calculation can be checked. A mortgage settlement statement alone does not establish the gain.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
CompletionRecord the actual date, rather than the estate-agent listing date.
Calculation inputsProvide acquisition, disposal, costs, ownership and relief information.
Separate tasksConfirm property reporting, payment and any annual-return entry.

Two more questions you may have

Does each joint owner report the whole gain?

Give the accountant the ownership details. Each owner’s reporting position needs checking; do not duplicate the full proceeds as each person’s own disposal.

Can I wait until I have every document before mentioning the sale?

Alert the accountant immediately and list the missing records. That allows the deadline and next steps to be addressed promptly.

  • Completion and exchange dates
  • Purchase and sale statements
  • Ownership shares and residence history
  • Fees, improvements and relevant relief evidence
  • Property report, payment and annual-return responsibilities
